species.name: Snapper
species.how: soft-baits or berleyed baits along reef edges and work-ups
notes: Inshore spawning aggregations Oct-Mar, peak Nov-Dec; spawning starts at roughly 14.8-16 C sea temperature.
sources: Parsons et al. 2014, 'Snapper (Chrysophrys auratus): a review of life history and key vulnerabilities in New Zealand', NZ J Marine & Freshwater Research 48(2). https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00288330.2014.892013
NIWA: spring spawning migrations at about 16 C. https://niwa.co.nz/news/will-it-be-fintastic-fishing-year

species.name: Kahawai
species.how: lures or soft-baits on surface work-ups

species.name: Kingfish
species.how: live-baits or jigs around pins and reefs
notes: Fisheries NZ: in Cook Strait kingfish are encountered mainly in summer, and from East Cape to Hawke Bay most kingfish fishing occurs in summer. Months here = NZ summer (Dec-Feb); the source gives seasons, not months.
sources: Holdsworth, McKenzie, Walsh, van der Straten & O Maolagain 2013, 'Catch-at-age of yellowtail kingfish (Seriola lalandi) caught by recreational fishers in KIN 1', NZ Fisheries Assessment Report 2013/3, p. 4 (citing Holdsworth et al. 2007). https://webstatic.niwa.co.nz/library/FAR-2013-3.pdf

warnings: Tides: LINZ secondary port Wharekahika / Hicks Bay, 20.7 km from the spot centre; times/heights derived from Gisborne with LINZ mean differences (HW +39 min, LW +39 min).

Sea temperature is the Open-Meteo marine model (all-hours mean; it includes daytime warming). Against NOAA Coral Reef Watch 5 km night-only satellite SST on 22-23 Oct 2026 it was within about +/-1.2 C at all 21 coastal spots, with no net bias at night (docs/SST_CHECK.md).
